messages:
jonathan: quick heads-up — product noticed a few customers getting mixed signals from our API when a request is routed to a cheaper model variant. They see 200 + a note in body, or sometimes 409, or a 202 with a retry hint. Confusing for SDKs and console UX.

tara: ugh. is this mostly routing fallbacks (expected) or a mix of rate/quota + fallback?

jonathan: mostly routing fallbacks + a couple quota edge cases where our proxy returns 409 for capacity gating. goal: one clear contract for callers so SDKs/console can show consistent badges/alerts.

mia: can we enumerate the concrete behaviours? i saw three patterns: 1) transparent fallback: 200 + body.metadata.fallback=true 2) surfaced status: 409 or 429 w/ message about capacity 3) async fallback: 202 accepted + note that we queued to a cooler model.

luis: we should avoid dual semantics where 200 sometimes means degraded. 200 should mean response content is final and acceptable. any degraded/combo state should map to a non-2xx code or a dedicated header so clients can opt in.

samira: agree. from console UX POV we want a single signal to power: badge (OK / Degraded / Fallback) + CTA (retry/upgrade/contactsales). ideal signal is small: maybe X-Redwood-Serving-Status with values: ok | routed-variant | degraded | queued.

jonathan: that header idea is neat. but policy: do we prefer supplementing status codes or replace some current 4xx? e.g., quota gating returns 409 today — should that stay 4xx or become 429 with extra code?

tara: 409 is ambiguous for clients. 429 already implies rate/quota and many clients have built-in retry heuristics for 429. Recommend normalizing gating -> 429 + X-Redwood-Reason=quota_exceeded. keep 409 for conflicting state changes (rare).

mia: routing fallback should not be a hard error. If we intentionally routed to a cheaper-but-compatible model, it could be 200 + header X-Redwood-Serving-Status=routed-variant. but also include X-Redwood-Quality=nominal|reduced so console can surface quality badge and link to logs.

luis: important: SDKs need stable machine-readable enums, not free text. we should publish a short contract and version it: Serving-Status v1. e.g., header values: ok, routed-variant, degraded, queued, failover.

samira: rollout plan: 1) bake header in hosted runtime (silent) for 2 weeks 2) update SDKs to surface badge when header present 3) console wiring + shortlines for customer-facing copy 4) opt-in to strict codes in 2 months.

jonathan: telemetry ask: capture both header and code, plus model variant id and latency delta. need that to correlate quality regressions and customer impact. create low-cardinality tags for console filters.

tara: open question: what about parity for Private/Dedicated where headers may be stripped by proxies? we need to document fallback: include body.metadata.serving_status in API response JSON as a fallback channel.

mia: sample console copy (short): "Routed to lower-cost model; output may vary. Learn more" and tooltip: "Automatically routed to a compatible model to maintain availability. See logs for model id and latency."

luis: SDK suggestion: expose Response.servingStatus enum + .servingMetadata map. default behavior: no automatic retries on 'routed-variant' unless app opts in.

jonathan: one more policy note: when behavior changes we must bump the header contract and add migration notes in changelog. please mock a short RFC and propose exact header names & enum values.

samira: noted — i'll draft console copy variations and the small UX mock for the badge. pinging infra-bot to open ticket for runtime header + telemetry pipeline.

infra-bot: Created issue PLAT-5219: "Serving-status header + telemetry for routed/quality states" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.

tara: thanks. next steps: jonathan + luis to spec header enums and error-code normalizations, mia + samira to draft copy & SDK shape. sync in 48h?

jonathan: +1. will start RFC today and paste a short diff in this thread.

mia: thx all :thumbsup:

samira: also adding a couple customer quotes about confusion to the ticket for context.

jonathan: putting a small note here: don't conflate 'degraded' with 'routed-variant' — degraded implies output quality loss; routed-variant could be functionally equivalent but cheaper. keep both as possible values.

luis: agreed. ok moving to write up.
